keyFindings.description: go.env names the warm module cache first (file://…|https://proxy.golang.org|direct). The copied cache holds an @v/list per module listing only the cached versions, and a `|` falls through only on an error, so `go get X@latest`, `go get -u`, `go list -m -u` and `go list -m -versions` answer from the cache in every repository a role opens. Reproduced: a cache holding golang.org/x/text v0.3.0 makes `go list -m -versions` print v0.3.0 alone, where proxy.golang.org gives v0.43.0 as @latest. Fix: delete the list (and any @latest) files from the copied cache, and assert none in the final-stage check.

Each copy is `crane copy <floating upstream tag> <registry>:<shared tag>`. A branch that refreshes a row moves the shared tag to its digest; every later ci-images run that does not carry the refresh then finds the tag off its row, copies the floating upstream (which lands at the new digest) and fails, and main's digest is left untagged, which is the retention risk the tag exists to stop. Fix: copy from <upstream repo>@<row digest>, and make each tag unique per digest.

Rule 3 refuses any oven/bun or library/golang row whose version is not the pin, so a Bun or Go bump must add the row and repoint every FROM in one commit; that commit's consumer jobs (worker-image, envoy-smoke, the Dockerfile builds) need only `changes` and pull the new digest while the ci-images job may still be copying it. The solution document says a row 'does not race its own gate' and 'Do not re-run the job', which is wrong for that case. Fix: let a row for the next version land before the pin (rule 3 requires a row for the pin and refuses a FROM on another version), say in ci-images.yaml, AGENTS.md and the solution document that a new row lands in a commit before its consumers, or order the consumers after ci-images.

main's #2498 (172dcb5d) moved this Postgres to PostgreSQL 18 (library/postgres@sha256:979bccfd…), the version CI and Cloud SQL run; the forward merge kept a postgres:16 row and digest instead, so the devbox proof now runs another major version. Fix: a row for docker.io/library/postgres@sha256:979bccfd…, the script pointed at it, the postgres-16 row deleted.
